problem.passage:
The mycologist Elena Voss spent three summers cataloging fungal networks beneath a single stretch of old-growth forest. Using DNA sequencing, she traced individual mycelial colonies across hundreds of meters, discovering that many trees she had assumed were competitors were instead linked by shared fungal threads. Voss ______ that these underground networks allow trees to exchange nutrients and even chemical warning signals when pests attack.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The mycologist Elena Voss spent three summers cataloging fungal networks beneath a single stretch of old-growth forest. Using DNA sequencing, she traced individual mycelial colonies across hundreds of meters, discovering that many trees she had assumed were competitors were instead linked by shared fungal threads. Voss ______ that these underground networks allow trees to exchange nutrients and even chemical warning signals when pests attack.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

distractorRationales.matches: the correct meaning (Voss reaching a conclusion)
distractorRationales.plausible_because: it carries the right sense of the verb 'conclude'
distractorRationales.why_wrong: "conclude" is a base/present form that does not agree with the singular subject in past context and leaves the sentence without a properly tensed main verb

distractorRationales.matches: the participle form often seen after a comma introducing a result
distractorRationales.plausible_because: -ing forms often follow a main clause to add detail, so it looks fluent
distractorRationales.why_wrong: "concluding" is a nonfinite participle and cannot serve as the sentence's main verb, leaving the clause without a predicate

distractorRationales.plausible_because: it suggests a completed action before another event, which seems logically plausible
distractorRationales.why_wrong: "having concluded" is also a nonfinite verb form and cannot function as the main verb of the independent clause

problem.evidenceSpan: Voss ______ that these underground networks allow trees to exchange nutrients
problem.answerRationale: The sentence needs a finite past-tense main verb to pair with the subject "Voss" and complete the independent clause, and "concluded" supplies exactly that.

difficultyReasons: 필요한 추론 단계: 1단계 - 문장에 본동사가 필요함을 인식하고 시제를 과거로 맞추면 됨
핵심 관계: 단순 문법 구조(본동사 vs 분사) 판별로 미묘한 의미 관계는 없음
오답 공유 정보: 세 오답 모두 동사가 아닌 형태(분사)라는 공통점을 공유하여 구별이 명확함
자료 해석 필요성: 별도 자료나 수식 해석 불필요, 순수 문법 판단

distractors.plausibleBecause: 동사 원형이라 주어 Voss 뒤에 바로 이어질 것 같은 느낌을 줄 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 주어가 3인칭 단수(Voss)이므로 동사 원형 'conclude'는 수 일치가 되지 않아 문장이 성립하지 않음 (concludes가 맞는 형태이나 이것도 과거 시제 문맥과 맞지 않음)

distractors.plausibleBecause: 현재분사형으로 문장에 자연스럽게 이어지는 듯한 리듬을 줄 수 있음
distractors.matches: 문장 앞부분의 'discovering'과 형태적으로 유사해 평행 구조처럼 보일 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 'concluding'은 분사형으로 본동사 역할을 할 수 없어 문장이 완전한 절이 되지 못하고 문법적으로 불완전함(주어 Voss에 대한 본동사가 없음)

distractors.plausibleBecause: 완료 분사구문으로 앞선 조사 과정을 마친 후의 상태를 나타내는 것처럼 보일 수 있음
distractors.matches: 앞 문장의 'spent three summers cataloging'과 시간적 순서상 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.whyWrong: 'having concluded'도 분사구문이라 본동사가 될 수 없으며, 문장에 필요한 주절의 동사가 없어 비문이 됨
